sections.title: Secret Seashells
sections.note: Game Boy and DX: 26. Get all of them before the Koholint Sword.

items.name: Bush north of the Trendy Game
items.area: Bush patch one screen north of the Trendy Game
items.howTo: Cut the bush four rows across and four rows up in the patch north of the Trendy Game.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Chest behind a rock
items.howTo: Lift the rock in front of the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: BowWow's doghouse
items.howTo: Dig in the bottom-right corner of BowWow's doghouse.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Tail Cave chest
items.howTo: From the entrance go up, left and up, bomb the cracked west wall and open the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Key Cavern roof
items.howTo: Climb the stairs one screen right of Key Cavern's entrance, go one screen left and dig the bare square between four tufts of grass.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Seashell Mansion: exactly 5
items.howTo: Walk into the Seashell Mansion carrying exactly 5 seashells and the sensor gives you one more.
items.notes: Lost if you pass 5 without visiting. Not in the Switch remake.

items.name: Bushes east of the Mansion
items.area: One screen right of the Seashell Mansion
items.howTo: It's under the second of the top two bushes.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Tunnel under Richard's Villa
items.area: Tunnel from Richard's Villa, left path
items.howTo: Give Richard the five Golden Leaves to open the tunnel. Take the left path, push the boulder into the pit, jump across and open the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Bush below the Witch's Hut
items.howTo: Lift the rock blocking the stairs, go down one screen, cut the lone bush and dig where it was.
items.notes: Zelda Dungeon's Game Boy page puts it in Ukuku Prairie. Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Tree by the phone booth
items.area: Telephone booth just east of Mabe Village
items.howTo: Dash into the tree by the phone booth with the Pegasus Boots.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Seashell Mansion: exactly 10
items.howTo: Walk into the Seashell Mansion carrying exactly 10 seashells and the sensor gives you one more.
items.notes: Lost if you pass 10 without visiting. Not in the Switch remake.

items.name: Tree by Tail Cave
items.howTo: Dash into the left side of the lone tree west of Tail Cave's entrance.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Bush by the Martha's Bay phone booth
items.area: South-west corner, by the phone booth
items.howTo: Cut the small bush in the corner by the phone booth.
items.notes: Zelda's Palace places it by the Mermaid Statue, across the lake, and needs the Power Bracelet. Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Owl Statue past the cave
items.area: Cave south-west of the Seashell Mansion
items.howTo: Bomb the cave's west wall, jump the pit and go out the far side, then dig one square down and one left of the Owl Statue.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Odd rock among the stones
items.area: North of Catfish's Maw, by the Moblins
items.howTo: Lift the one liftable rock among the ring-shaped stones.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Desert boulder
items.howTo: Lift the lower of the two boulders.
items.notes: Zelda's Palace lists the Pegasus Boots. Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: House by the Bay pots
items.howTo: Lift the bottom-right pot inside the house.
items.notes: Zelda Dungeon says it appears only after you help the Ghost; Zelda's Palace says it's there either way. Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Martha's Bay islet
items.area: Islet west of the House by the Bay
items.howTo: Swim to the islet and cut its bush.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Islet by Key Cavern
items.howTo: Swim to the islet and slash its bush from the north side.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Owl Statue across the bridge
items.area: Two screens south and one west of Animal Village's entrance
items.howTo: Cross the bridge and dig just left of the Owl Statue.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Armos stairs
items.howTo: Touch the lower-right of the four Armos statues to reveal stairs, and open the chest below.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Face Shrine island
items.howTo: Take the stairs in Face Shrine's north-west room out to an island in the rapids and open the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Over the potholes west of Kanalet
items.howTo: Carry the Flying Rooster and fly west from the gate across the potholes, then take the stairs to the chest.
items.notes: On Switch you Hookshot across instead. Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Rock east of the Hen House
items.howTo: Cross the bridge east of the Hen House and lift the corner rock.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Shallow-water cave
items.area: Cave on the way to Eagle's Tower
items.howTo: Bomb your way in, push the blocks past the Rupee chests, come out the far side and open the chest outside.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Eagle's Tower walkway
items.howTo: Go left one, up one, take the stairs, down one, drop into the top-left pit onto the walkway, then up two screens to the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Switch remake.

items.name: Koholint Sword
items.howTo: Bring 20 or more seashells to the Seashell Mansion.
items.notes: The original's only Mansion reward. Once you have it, seashells still out in the world are gone or turn into 20 Rupees (Zelda Wiki), so collect all 26 first.

sections.title: Switch Seashells
sections.note: The 2019 Switch remake: 50 (24 of the original's and 26 new). Counted apart from the Game Boy and DX total.

items.name: Bush north of the Trendy Game
items.area: 6×6 bush patch north of the Trendy Game
items.howTo: Cut the bushes in the patch.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Trendy Game: first seashell
items.howTo: Win it from the crane game once the Yoshi Doll and first Piece of Heart are gone.

items.name: Chest behind a rock
items.howTo: Lift the boulder in front of the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: BowWow's doghouse
items.howTo: Dig in the bottom-right corner of the doghouse.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Tail Cave chest
items.howTo: Go up, left and up, bomb the west wall and open the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions. Bombs are sold only after Bottle Grotto on Switch (Zelda's Palace), so it comes later.

items.name: Bush below the Witch's Hut
items.howTo: Lift the stone, cut the lone bush and dig where it was.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Bushes east of the Mansion
items.howTo: Cut the bushes east of the Seashell Mansion.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Odd rock among the stones
items.howTo: Lift the lone liftable rock among the fixed stones.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Owl Statue past the cave
items.area: Cave south-west of the Seashell Mansion
items.howTo: Bomb the cave's west wall, go out the far side and dig south-west of the Owl Statue.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Bush by the Martha's Bay phone booth
items.area: Corner just east of the phone booth
items.howTo: Cut the bush in the corner.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Under the big skull
items.area: South-west of Kanalet Castle, east of Mabe
items.howTo: Bomb the big skull and dig where it stood.

items.name: Ring of blue flowers
items.howTo: Dig in the middle of the ring.

items.name: North-west of the forest
items.howTo: Dig along the west wall by the trees.
items.notes: Nintendo Life also lists Roc's Feather.

items.name: By Mr. Write's phone booth
items.area: West end, by the phone booth near Mr. Write's House
items.howTo: Cut the bush and dig.
items.notes: Nintendo Life and Zelda's Palace also list Roc's Feather.

items.name: Rock by the sign
items.area: East of Bottle Grotto, north of the Moblin Hideout
items.howTo: Lift the right-hand rock by the sign.

items.name: Tabahl Wasteland east edge
items.howTo: Dig along the east edge.

items.name: Hole by the warp point
items.howTo: Throw a bomb into the hole next to the warp point.

items.name: By the log on the beach
items.area: East end of the beach, by the log
items.howTo: Dig in the far lower-left corner.

items.name: Tunnel under Richard's Villa
items.area: Tunnel from Richard's Villa, left path
items.howTo: Take the left path, push the block, jump across and open the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Key Cavern roof
items.howTo: Dig between the four tufts of grass.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Desert Owl Statue
items.howTo: Dig just south of the statue, by the cactus.

items.name: Desert boulder
items.howTo: Lift the lower of the two rocks.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Where the Walrus lay
items.howTo: Play the Ballad of the Wind Fish where the Walrus was.

items.name: Owl Statue across the bridge
items.howTo: Dig just west of the Owl Statue.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions. Zelda Dungeon also lists the Flippers.

items.name: Armos stairs
items.howTo: Touch the bottom-right of the four Armos to reveal stairs, and open the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions. The Bow (or Boomerang) makes the Armos easier.

items.name: Lone boulder north of the ruins
items.area: North of the Ancient Ruins, east of the Face Shrine
items.howTo: Lift the lone north-east boulder.
items.notes: Zelda Dungeon lists the Flippers and Zelda's Palace the Pegasus Boots for getting there.

items.name: Dampé: four challenges
items.howTo: Complete four of Dampé's Chamber Dungeon challenges.

items.name: Tree by the phone booth
items.area: Phone booth east of Mabe Village
items.howTo: Dash into the tree with the Pegasus Boots.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Tree by Tail Cave
items.howTo: Dash into the lone tree.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Palm tree on the beach
items.howTo: Dash into the lower of the four palm trees.

items.name: Kanalet moat waterfall
items.area: Moat, at the foot of the waterfall
items.howTo: Dive at the foot of the moat's waterfall.

items.name: House by the Bay pots
items.howTo: Lift the pots at the bottom right.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Trendy Game: second seashell
items.howTo: Win it from the crane game.

items.name: Martha's Bay islet
items.howTo: Swim out and cut its bush.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Christine's thanks
items.howTo: Talk to Christine after delivering her letter to Mr. Write in the trading sequence.

items.name: Islet by Key Cavern
items.howTo: Swim out and cut its bush.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: The Secret Zora
items.howTo: Look at the Zora in the north-east house through the Magnifying Lens.

items.name: Over the potholes west of Kanalet
items.howTo: Hookshot over the potholes and take the stairs to the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions. The original needs the Flying Rooster.

items.name: Rapids Ride: empty islet
items.howTo: On a free ride, go far west then south, Hookshot to the vines on the empty islet and dig its top-right corner.

items.name: Rapids Race
items.howTo: Finish the Rapids Race in 35 seconds or less.
items.notes: 35 s per Zelda Dungeon and Nintendo Life. The race costs 100 Rupees.

items.name: Face Shrine island
items.howTo: Take the stairs out to an island in the rapids and open the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Fishing Pond: a Cheep Cheep
items.howTo: Catch a Cheep Cheep.

items.name: Fishing Pond: a Blooper or a big fish
items.howTo: Catch a Blooper, or any fish of 100–150 cm (Ol' Baron counts).
items.notes: Nintendo Life says after Face Shrine. The Blooper also gives the Heavyweight Lure.

items.name: Waterfall by the big ladder
items.area: Where the waterfall to Angler's Tunnel was
items.howTo: Dive by the waterfall beside the big ladder.

items.name: Hole under the bridge
items.area: Bridge west of the Hen House
items.howTo: Throw a bomb into the hole under the bridge.
items.notes: Zelda Dungeon also lists the Power Bracelet and Flippers.

items.name: Rock east of the Hen House
items.area: East across the bridge from the Hen House
items.howTo: Lift the rightmost of the three rocks.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Shallow-water cave
items.howTo: Bomb the north wall, push the blocks, go out and open the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Eagle's Tower walkway
items.howTo: Drop down a left hole in the Hinox room to the raised walkway and open the chest.
items.notes: Also in the Game Boy and DX versions.

items.name: Rock past the rockfall
items.area: West of the Wind Fish's Egg, past the rockfall
items.howTo: Lift the north-east rock.
items.notes: Nintendo Life lists the Power Bracelet.

items.name: Cross of stones by Turtle Rock
items.area: Just east of Turtle Rock's entrance
items.howTo: Dig in the middle of the cross of small stones.

sections.title: Switch Mansion
sections.note: Rewards at 5, 15, 30, 40 and 50; no exact count needed, and two can come in one visit.

items.name: 5 seashells
items.howTo: Bring 5 seashells.
items.notes: Also in Heart Pieces, on its Switch tab.

items.name: 15 seashells
items.howTo: Bring 15 seashells.

items.name: 30 seashells
items.howTo: Bring 30 seashells.

items.name: 40 seashells
items.howTo: Bring 40 seashells.

items.name: 50 seashells
items.howTo: Bring all 50 seashells.
items.notes: 300 Rupees per Zelda Wiki; Zelda's Palace says 280 and Nintendo Life names only the Chamber Stone.
